parsed.reason: This message hits all required elements for an optin-type introduction perfectly. It uses first-person singular ("I can make an introduction"), is grammatically correct, and reads like a competent chief of staff. It directly addresses the parent's primary concern—"what did you tell them?"—by explicitly stating nothing is shared until both families agree. It includes the off-ramp ("You can turn it off anytime"), mentions other families nearby without inventing specifics, and conditions the introduction on genuine matching ("when the ages line up"). No announcement voice, no exclamation marks, no directive language telling them what to type back, no overselling. The tone is reassuring and matter-of-fact, treating this as the small thing it is.
